hints: Look first at the letters used in each option. Remember mRNA never contains T, and the order must be histidine, then proline, then aspartic acid, then leucine.
The table gives DNA template triplets, so build each mRNA codon by complementary pairing: DNA G pairs with C, DNA C pairs with G, DNA T pairs with A, and DNA A pairs with U.
walkthrough:
**Spot what mRNA must look like**

mRNA uses bases A, U, C and G only. It has no T. It is made by complementary base pairing to the DNA template strand.

Pairing rule:
$$DNA\ G \to mRNA\ C,\ DNA\ C \to mRNA\ G,\ DNA\ T \to mRNA\ A,\ DNA\ A \to mRNA\ U$$

**Transcribe each amino acid in order**

Work through histidine-proline-aspartic acid-leucine using the table.

Histidine GTA becomes CAU, and GTG becomes CAC. Proline GGA becomes CCU, and GGG becomes CCC. Aspartic acid CTA becomes GAU, and CTG becomes GAC. Leucine GAT becomes CUA, and GAC becomes CUG.

**Match to the options**

Option B gives ...CAU CCU GAC CUA... This is CAU for histidine (from GTA), CCU for proline (from GGA), GAC for aspartic acid (from CTG), and CUA for leucine (from GAT). Every codon fits perfectly, in the correct order.

options.A: Close but not correct. The third codon GAA codes for glutamic acid, not aspartic acid, so it does not match CTA or CTG.
options.B: Correct. Each codon is the true mRNA complement of a listed DNA triplet, in the right order for histidine, proline, aspartic acid and leucine.
options.C: Incorrect. It contains T, so it is DNA, not mRNA. It just copies the DNA triplets GTA, CCA is not even listed, and so on.
options.D: Incorrect. It copies the DNA bases instead of pairing complementarily, for example GTA becomes GUA instead of CAU.
